_README: Per-client Amazon Account Audit config. Copy to config.<client>-<market>.json (gitignored; only this TEMPLATE is committed). Fill every <...> placeholder. Paths in inputs{} may use ~ and repo-relative paths. Run: python tools/amazon-ad-audit/build_audit.py --config <this file> --preflight, then --config <this file> to build. Break-even ACOS is an ASSUMPTION until margin is confirmed; every red/amber verdict keys off it.
client_price_note: Optional but strongly recommended. The client's REAL selling price. Keyword research reports the live offer, often the BUY BOX price, so during a hijack or stock-out it is a third party's and puts the client in the wrong place on the price/rating chart. Leave null to derive ASP from the Business Report (sales / units). client_dtc_price adds the brand's own-website price as a reference line.
brand_tokens_note: Substring, case-insensitive. Include real misspellings that carry brand intent; do NOT include dictionary words that merely resemble the brand.
core_tokens: <category phrase the product actually competes on>
core_tokens_note: Optional. Splits GENERIC into winnable CORE vs undifferentiated HEAD for the SQP demand figures. Without it every generic term counts as core, i.e. the old two-way behaviour. Include the category language a shopper uses for THIS product ('under eye brightener'); leave OUT the shelf above it ('makeup', 'beauty'). Head terms are real demand but no single listing wins them, so counting them as addressable overstates the category by an order of magnitude and makes category share look far worse than it is.
asin_groups_note: Optional. null or {} for an ungrouped single-line catalog. Groups map SQP files and Business-Report ASINs to product lines.

windows.research: <YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD of the SoldScope keyword research; leave empty to take it from research.json>

comparison_windows.disruption: <optional incident/suppression window; leave empty for a clean run>
comparison_windows.online_control: <optional latest four complete weeks continuously online>
comparison_windows.note: Keep incident and online-control windows separate. Do not blend them.

research._note: The SoldScope keyword research run behind the organic overlay. Leave asins empty to skip it. One run covers 2 to 10 ASINs and has no persistent niche. Legacy configs use datadive_niche, inputs.datadive_niche_json, inputs.datadive_competitors_json, inputs.rank_radar_json and windows.datadive; those keys still build.

inputs.search_catalog_performance_csv: <optional Search Catalog Performance .csv for product-level funnel validation>
inputs.research_json: <path to research.json from tools/soldscope/keywords.py (keywords + competitors in one file), or empty>
inputs.rank_series_json: <optional path to a rank series from tools/soldscope/ranks.py (keyword + ranks over time) for the standard fig_rank_movement chart, or empty>
inputs.market_sizing_json: <optional directional market-size appendix JSON; set its provider field (soldscope) so the appendix names the source>
inputs.voice_guide_path: <optional writing authority used when authoring the client narrative; never embedded in the deliverable>

delivery.drive_folder: {drive}/04_Sales Audits/<Client>   (token resolves per machine; never an absolute path)

narrative.mode_note: Use evidence_hybrid when the operator asks for the same style as UltimaPeak.

branding._note: Branded rendering creates an A4 DOCX intermediate for conversion to the sole deliverable: a native Google Doc. After conversion, run the native normalization in native_doc_normalize.py so a deep audit has a full-page cover, no first-page furniture, and a right-aligned content header. Agency identity comes from _local/branding/branding.json; see tools/amazon-ad-audit/BRANDING.md. first_time=true renders the cover; regular update audits set false. Requires the local brand assets. Falls back to plain md_to_docx if assets or Chrome are missing.
branding.cover_subtitle: A straight look at the account, with recommendations on where to start.
